Updated the Phase 6 heading in the plan from [NOT STARTED] to [PARTIAL] with a full resolution note; checked off the PREFLIGHT, intUniverse/intWork, and build/commit checklist items; left the intExpandBranches_world_bound item unchecked with a DEFERRED annotation. NOT landed: intExpandBranches_world_bound (the '(b.map (.label)).eraseDups.length <= phi.complexity + 1' bound). Investigation (not a stub attempt -- genuine mathematical analysis) found: worlds are created ONLY by the F(phi->psi) world-creating rule (persistence only ever copies T-signed formulas, never F-signed, so it cannot itself create or duplicate a world-creation opportunity). However, F-and and T-or are BETA (branching) rules while F-or and T-and are ALPHA (non-branching, same-branch) rules in this calculus (confirmed by reading Rules.lean's IBranchSaturation field statements directly, not assumed) -- so a SINGLE branch's full history can still accumulate multiple sibling worlds at the same depth whenever multiple F-imp obligations are combined via ALPHA-decomposable connectives (e.g. phi = (a1->b1) or (a2->b2) or ... or (ak->bk), since F-or is alpha, decomposes to k simultaneous F-imp obligations at world 0 on ONE branch, each firing to create its own child world). The bound is still true (each additional or/and connective 'pays' complexity budget covering the extra branching-adjacent world), but proving it rigorously requires a genuine occurrence-tracking argument -- e.g. that each world-creation event consumes a DISTINCT syntactic .imp occurrence within phi (tied to the monotonically-growing, never-reprocessed 'expanded' set already threaded through the recursion for other invariants, e.g. the existing private ILabelBound/IExpandedConsistent infrastructure at Scheme.lean:913 onward) -- NOT a simple ancestor-chain depth argument. This is comparable in difficulty to Phase 7's intExpMeasure_step_lt (both require new invariants threaded through the full intExpandBranches/go nested well-founded recursion) and was not force-fit into this single dispatch, per the plan's explicit 'land partial + continuation' escape valve when the world-bound proof balloons.
